blind_comparisons.not_possible_reason: RI-AI05's blind pair asks a critic to cluster ten unlabelled 90-second behaviour fingerprints into roles. The shipped roster has five statblocks and one behavioural role, so ten distinct fingerprints cannot be drawn and the clustering question is answered by the census before it is asked. Running it would have been a vacuous pass (RULES 4).

checks.observed: Engine.applySave() and Engine.loadState() BOTH call population.reset() (every post -> DORMANT) and sim.souls.reset() (the eid ledger the S5 epoch gate is keyed on -> empty), while death.ordinaryRespawnEpoch does not move. A save and a load is not a rest and costs no world clock. The builder's A8 proved walking away and coming back is correctly refused; the save/load door has not been tried by anybody.
checks.why_unmeasured: my C3 arm's first run killed bodies by writing hp on the sim.entities record and fetching a combat body through a non-existent accessor (E.combat.bodies.get; the real one is combat.bodyOf). sim/combat-bridge.js#mirror rewrote e.hp from the live combat body on the next step, so the kill un-happened and the arm reported killed:2 / delta:0. Fixed in the tool; the re-run did not land inside budget.

checks.observed: HP, damage, poise, reach, sight radius and moveset are identical for a given statblock in every tier — the placement varies WHICH statblock stands where and never its numbers. PopulationSystem reads no player level, region-clear count or playtime.
checks.note: This is the thing the piece got structurally right and it is the constraint most likely to be broken by a 'fix' for §3 or §4. Any remedy that raises tier difficulty by touching a statblock's HP or damage per region is an AR-1 automatic fail.

checks.observed: This piece places bodies and streams them; it takes no frame decision inside a fight. The one frame-budget risk it carries — up to four engine.spawn() calls when a post materialises — is bounded by spawn_per_step:1 and was not measured here, because no timing figure is claimed anywhere in this verdict (loadavg 12-22 throughout).
checks.why: ARBITRATION S26 forbids diluting AR-1 to cover ordinary defects. The defects found here are economy and fairness defects, not Morrowind-side subsystems setting the schedule of a Souls-side one.

ar1.not_applicable_reason: This piece places bodies and streams them; it takes no frame decision inside a fight, and it installs nothing on the combat schedule. Its one frame-budget risk — up to four engine.spawn() calls when a post materialises — is bounded by the model's own spawn_per_step: 1 and by max_resident_posts: 14, and it was deliberately NOT measured here because the box carried 18-36 concurrent browsers at loadavg 12-22 throughout and no timing figure is claimed anywhere in this verdict (RULES 26). ARBITRATION S26 forbids diluting AR-1 to cover ordinary defects: the three defects this verdict finds are an economy violation, a fairness violation and a legibility failure, none of which is a Morrowind-side subsystem taking a frame decision away from the fight. Flagged for round 2 on a quiet box: a post materialising four bodies inside an active fight is the one place this piece could become an AR-1 question, and nobody has measured it.

checks.observed: 267 placed bodies across 13 regions did not cost the Souls side anything structural: statblocks are byte-unchanged, the two existing encounter behaviour rules are byte-unchanged (the third, always_hostile, is additive), respawn.json is untouched, and no enemy stat varies by region (S9 holds).
checks.why: The breadth this piece adds is placement, not new systems competing with the fight.

score.band_label: The province is populated; the danger tier is a label
score.aggregation_note: mean of RI-AI05 2 (capped by two triggered hard fails), RI-PRG06 2 (min-over-axes; an unbounded save/load farm plus band separation = 0), RI-MTH07 6, RI-AI07 8 => 4.5 -> 4.
score.confidence: HIGH on every placement-data finding (§2, §3, §4 — all re-derived from the shipped tree with a script that shares no code with the builder's); HIGH on the two controls and the six-probe diagnostic; NOT CLAIMED on survivability, on the felt density of a walked crossing, or on the save/load soul door.

status_reasons: ARBITRATION S5 violation, driven with a control that went the other way: a save and a load re-pays every corpse in the province at an unmoved epoch, without bound and without a hearth rest (+98 souls on the re-kill of pop-0001). It defeats a fix a neighbouring piece built specifically in response to this one.
RI-AI05 M4's introduction rule hard-fails in BOTH directions of the game's own canonical critical-path route, and the piece explicitly claimed that rule in its own model file.

RI-PRG06 aggregates min-over-axes and band separation scores 0: adjacent tiers overlap 67-100% against a <=25% threshold, so 'which region am I in' is not answerable from a kill anywhere in the province.
94% of placed bodies sit outside their region tier's soul band, and the realised tier gradient (1.97x at t5) is a twelfth of the contract's 24.4x, and non-monotone with t5 below t4.
The tier is flat on the axes the model declares: tier_multiplier range 1.29x and non-monotone; median road spacing IDENTICAL at 140 m in tiers 2, 3 and 5.
The design half of the shipped model has no demonstrated file->world consumer; the arm that would show it was attempted three times by the builder and never obtained.

AGAINST all of that, and it is substantial: the defect the piece was sent to close IS closed, and I confirmed it on a walk the builder never took. 9 hand-typed bodies became 267 streamed ones; 5,999.4 m of the crossing materialises 32 posts and releases 31 behind the player with 0 faults; the composition gradient is real and legible in play; the consumer is in the correct slot and province-cell gated; all four declared density figures are inside their bands; and the roster gap was declared rather than hidden. This is a FAIL on the reference items, not a judgement that the work is poor.

biggest_gap.what: Engine.applySave() and Engine.loadState() both call PopulationSystem.reset(), which sets all 144 posts back to DORMANT, while SoulsSystem.reset() empties the eid ledger the S5 epoch gate is keyed on and death.ordinaryRespawnEpoch never moves. Measured at aaa2f1f on pop-0001, with no hearth rest and no harness respawn verb anywhere: L1 kill 2 bodies -> +98 souls; L2 CONTROL walk out past release_radius_m and back -> post stays CLEARED, 0 bodies, delta 0 (correctly refused); L3 saveState -> loadState -> the post re-materialises with 2 bodies -> kill again -> +98 souls with the epoch unmoved at 0. Repeatable without bound.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: ARBITRATION S5 and RI-PRG06 §4 both price a respawn at a rest, and the rest is what makes the world clock cost something. This removes the price. RI-PRG06 exists because 'a soul curve without a soul supply is unfalsifiable', and an unbounded farm makes the supply unfalsifiable again; its own 'How we lose' says 'every number in this file is instantly fiction', and RI-AI05 M6 fails at a farm rate >= 3x the clear rate. It also defeats a fix a neighbouring piece built SPECIFICALLY in response to this one: SoulsSystem's header names W1-POPULATION as the reason the boolean re-arm became an epoch gate, and the gate holds against the door that piece anticipated (the walk, proved by the builder's A8 and reproduced as my L2 control) and not against the one this piece opened. The population.reset() call is this piece's line, added by this piece, with its justification written on it: 'which ordinary mobs are dead is exactly what S5 says a rest restores anyway.' S5 says a REST restores them; a load is not a rest.

remedy.action: On applySave, restore each post's CLEARED/DORMANT state from the save instead of resetting all 144 posts to DORMANT — which is also what a player expects, since a reloaded save should not hand back a province they had already cleared. If persisting post state is out of scope for round 2, the narrower alternative is to have SoulsSystem's first-sight seed record a body as SETTLED at the current epoch when its post was recorded cleared in the save.
remedy.acceptance: Re-run tools/world/critic-population-r1.mjs --arms C3. All three legs must hold: L1 delta > 0 (a first kill pays), L2 delta == 0 (walking away and back is refused, as it is today), and L3 delta == 0 with death.ordinaryRespawnEpoch unmoved — where it is +98 today. Then a hearth rest must still re-arm: restAt() bumps the epoch and the next kill of the same post pays again.

secondary_observations.what: RUNNER-UP GAP, and a hard fail in its own right. The introduction rule is enforced against a table sorted by (danger_tier, distance-from-safety) instead of against a walked route. On roads.json named_routes.crossing, guard_legion debuts in a pair (forward) or a line of three (reverse, the direction the shipped default start forces) and drowned_lesser debuts in a pair.
secondary_observations.why_it_matters: RI-AI05 §D and M4 both call it a hard fail: 'an archetype whose first appearance is in a gank has not been taught, only survived.' The builder saw the walk-order problem and re-sorted the TAG rather than moving the POST, which is RULES 7 exactly.
secondary_observations.remedy: walk named_routes.crossing from the shipped default start, tag the first WALKED instance of each archetype, and move the post where that instance is a group; then assert it in tools/check-*.mjs (RULES 13, 14).

secondary_observations.what: PopulationSystem.reset() restores state, live, focus, epochSeen, stats and candidates. It does NOT restore `enabled`. reset() runs on every loadState and applySave, so setPopulation({enabled:false}) survives every scenario boundary for the life of the page.
secondary_observations.why_it_matters: Not player-facing — setPopulation is a harness verb — but worse than that for this project's method. Any suite that ablates the population and then loads a state measures a silently empty province that reports dormant:144 and looks exactly like a world nobody has walked into. It cost this critique its C1 arm and very nearly produced a false headline that the pump had stopped firing (see §5.1). RULES 4 has a twin: a probe that cannot succeed.
secondary_observations.remedy: one line in reset(); plus an arm that ablates must re-arm and ASSERT it is armed.

secondary_observations.what: reset() also does not clear this.faults, so populationReport().faults accumulates across every loadState for the life of the page.
secondary_observations.why_it_matters: my ablation arm, which spawned nothing at all, reported faults:2 inherited from two arms earlier. It will read as 'two posts in the province are unbuildable' to the next agent who looks.

secondary_observations.what: From the shipped default start the crossing runs t1 western-rootlands -> t2 blackwood -> t5 deep-marshes -> t3 stone-forest -> t4 valus-ridge -> t3 salt-hills. The player's THIRD region on the critical path is the highest tier in the game.
secondary_observations.why_it_matters: Lethality gating rather than level gating is correct and is ARBITRATION S9. What makes it fair in Souls is the introduction rule and a legible tier, and this verdict finds both broken. Flagged for W1-27's `coherence.difficulty.continuity` rather than scored here.

secondary_observations.what: RI-PRG06 §7's road slice (278-477 bodies) and RI-WLD02 D9's 0.7-1.2 groups per WILDERNESS minute cannot both be satisfied on the shipped trunk road; 46.4% of the trunk's 209 minutes is deliberately-clear settlement and hearth apron.
secondary_observations.why_it_matters: Confirmed, and confirmed as NOT this piece's to resolve. The builder shipped 267 — 4% under RI-PRG06's floor — and did not inflate the garrison rings to close the gap. That restraint was correct and should not be undone by a round-2 fix chasing the census number.

gap_closure.note: Independently verified with an instrument the builder did not write, at four coordinates the builder did not use (the shipped default start, pop-0001, the crossing route head, and tier-5 pop-0042), and falsified two ways: an ablation walk of 1,199.4 m yielding 0 posts, and a still control with drift ASSERTED at 0.00 m yielding 0 posts. 9 bodies -> 267.

path_to_ten.what: Sort the introduction pass by TRAVERSAL, not by tier.
path_to_ten.how: Walk named_routes.crossing from the shipped default start, then the remaining legs in road order, and tag the first WALKED instance of each archetype. Where the first walked instance is a group, MOVE THE POST — demote it to the solo template and promote a solo post upstream. Then assert it in tools/check-*.mjs so it cannot silently regress, arming the assertion only after the data satisfies it (RULES 13, RULES 14).

path_to_ten.what: Make the tier legible from one kill.
path_to_ten.how: Re-weight the composition tables so adjacent tiers draw from disjoint slices of the roster — t1 {24,34}, t2 {34,64}, t3 {64}, t4 {83}, t5 {157}. That takes the realised souls-per-body spread from 2.37x to about 5.4x and restores monotonicity, with NO new statblock and NO new soul value. Highest value available to this piece today and it costs one table.

path_to_ten.what: Build one archetype, not one hundred more bodies.
path_to_ten.how: A RANGED body is the single change that moves RI-AI05 most: required at 10-12% in EVERY region, named as §D's most-likely silent drop ('How we lose' #4), and the only way this placement can ever ask a second question. It is W1-12's path; this verdict's job is to say that 267 bodies of one question is not a roster.
path_to_ten.closes: RI-AI05 M1 / M3 / the roster-size hard fail

path_to_ten.what: Drive the crossing end to end at the level it pays, with no top-ups, and publish where the walker falls.
path_to_ten.how: The crossing's 38 bodies are worth 2,149 souls = level 5 on the shipped curve. That is the survivability number this critique owes and could not take.
path_to_ten.closes: the unmeasured half of this verdict

path_to_ten.what: Close arm A5 and the save/load door.
path_to_ten.how: A5 (perturb the model file, regenerate, reboot, re-census) is the only demonstration that the DESIGN half of the model reaches the world; it now costs two browser boots and no walking. Then kill a post, save, load, re-kill, and prove the S5 epoch gate holds through applySave as well as through a walk.

path_to_ten.how: Two lines. The first stops a whole class of neighbouring suite from silently measuring an empty province.

corpus_extended.what: §2's tier soul bands have no stated owner for the PLACEMENT side of the contract. §7 assigns the enemy census to RI-WLD07/RI-WLD02 and the soul budget to RI-PRG06, but nothing says who is responsible for a body of the right value standing in the right tier — which is the join, and is where this piece failed. Filed as an observation for the corpus owners rather than an edit.

method_deviations.deviation: Three tools were written by this critic under orchestration/TOOL-LOOP.md rule 1 and are cited as evidence: tools/world/critic-population-r1.mjs (arms C1 crossing walk, C2 still+ablation controls, C3 the save/load soul door, C4 a tier-5 fight), tools/world/critic-population-r1-diag.mjs (the six-probe diagnostic that proved the pump lives), and tools/world/critic-population-r1-shot.mjs (the image, drawn from the shipped data with pngjs, no browser).
method_deviations.why: The only population probe in the tree is tools/world/population-consumption.mjs, which is the builder's own. Nothing in the tree asks whether the introduction rule holds along a WALKED route, whether the tier gradient is legible, or whether a corpse can be re-paid through a save/load. None of my tools import the builder's; the placement findings are recomputed from the shipped JSON independently of the generator's own report block, and where the two agree (16,335 souls, 144 posts, 267 bodies) the verdict says so.
The pack cannot be assembled from a five-statblock, one-role roster; running it would be vacuous. Recorded rather than faked.

Arm C4 stood the player ~14 m from pop-0042 and swung 424 times across 240 sim-seconds: HP 620 -> 620, 8 bodies alive at start and 8 at the end, and the passive control byte-identical. self_audit.self_audit_note: ran_every_assigned_method is FALSE and this verdict is provisional on the points in `unmeasured`. The findings it rests on are driven: §2's farm is a three-leg arm whose control refused correctly, and §6.2's crossing walk is 5,999.4 m of real locomotion with the population system's armed state ASSERTED at the start. Two things a reader should weigh against me. First, my own C1 arm produced a spectacular false negative — 5,999.4 m of empty road — and I ran a six-probe diagnostic BEFORE filing it; had I filed it, this verdict's headline would have been that the population pump had stopped firing, which is false. The diagnostic instead surfaced OBS-population-reset-drops-enabled, a real defect. Second, arm C4 is void by my own badly-posed fixture, and it is void in exactly the way the builder warned about in its notes_for_successor, which I had read. Both are reported in §6 rather than quietly dropped. blind_done_where_required is FALSE by deliberate refusal: RI-AI05's blind pair is unassemblable on a five-statblock roster.
